deck.title: Requirements for Connecting to a Network

front_blocks.md: Define **IP address**.

back_blocks.md: An IP (Internet Protocol) address is a **unique identifier** given to devices which communicate over the **internet (WAN)**, making it possible to **deliver data to the right device**.

cards.front_md: Define **IP address**.
cards.back_md: An IP (Internet Protocol) address is a **unique identifier** given to devices which communicate over the **internet (WAN)**, making it possible to **deliver data to the right device**.

front_blocks.md: How is an IP address allocated to a device?

back_blocks.md: It can be allocated **by a network administrator** or assigned **dynamically by a DHCP server**.

cards.front_md: How is an IP address allocated to a device?
cards.back_md: It can be allocated **by a network administrator** or assigned **dynamically by a DHCP server**.

front_blocks.md: How is an IPv4 address written?

back_blocks.md: IPv4 is written as **4 blocks of denary numbers between 0 and 255**, separated by **full stops**, with each block one byte and each address 4 bytes.

cards.front_md: How is an IPv4 address written?
cards.back_md: IPv4 is written as **4 blocks of denary numbers between 0 and 255**, separated by **full stops**, with each block one byte and each address 4 bytes.

front_blocks.md: How is an IPv6 address written?

back_blocks.md: IPv6 is written as **8 blocks of 4 hexadecimal digits**, separated by **colons**, with each block 2 bytes and each address 16 bytes.

cards.front_md: How is an IPv6 address written?
cards.back_md: IPv6 is written as **8 blocks of 4 hexadecimal digits**, separated by **colons**, with each block 2 bytes and each address 16 bytes.

front_blocks.md: Why was IPv6 needed?

back_blocks.md: IPv4 provides just over **4 billion unique addresses**, which is not enough for over **7 billion people** with countless devices each.

cards.front_md: Why was IPv6 needed?
cards.back_md: IPv4 provides just over **4 billion unique addresses**, which is not enough for over **7 billion people** with countless devices each.

front_blocks.md: Define **MAC address**.

back_blocks.md: A MAC (Media Access Control) address is a **universally unique identifier** given to devices which communicate over a **local area network (LAN)**.

cards.front_md: Define **MAC address**.
cards.back_md: A MAC (Media Access Control) address is a **universally unique identifier** given to devices which communicate over a **local area network (LAN)**.

front_blocks.md: When is a MAC address assigned to a device?

back_blocks.md: Any device containing a **Network Interface Card (NIC)** has a MAC address **assigned during manufacturing**.

cards.front_md: When is a MAC address assigned to a device?
cards.back_md: Any device containing a **Network Interface Card (NIC)** has a MAC address **assigned during manufacturing**.

front_blocks.md: How is a MAC address written, and what do its parts mean?

back_blocks.md: A MAC address is **12 hexadecimal digits** grouped in pairs; the **first three pairs are the manufacturer ID number (OUI)** and the **last three pairs are the serial number** of the network interface card.

cards.front_md: How is a MAC address written, and what do its parts mean?
cards.back_md: A MAC address is **12 hexadecimal digits** grouped in pairs; the **first three pairs are the manufacturer ID number (OUI)** and the **last three pairs are the serial number** of the network interface card.

front_blocks.md: Give three uses of a MAC address.

back_blocks.md: MAC addresses can **restrict or allow access to a network**, **identify a device** on a network, **track a device**, and **assign static or fixed IP addresses**.

cards.front_md: Give three uses of a MAC address.
cards.back_md: MAC addresses can **restrict or allow access to a network**, **identify a device** on a network, **track a device**, and **assign static or fixed IP addresses**.

front_blocks.md: MAC addresses make it possible for <u>**            **</u> to efficiently forward data to the intended recipient.

back_blocks.md: MAC addresses make it possible for **switches** to efficiently forward data to the intended recipient.

front_blocks.md: Describe two differences between IP addresses and MAC addresses.

back_blocks.md: An IP address is **dynamic and can change** while a MAC address is **static and cannot change**; an IP address is used to communicate on a **WAN or the internet** while a MAC address is used on a **LAN**.

cards.front_md: Describe two differences between IP addresses and MAC addresses.
cards.back_md: An IP address is **dynamic and can change** while a MAC address is **static and cannot change**; an IP address is used to communicate on a **WAN or the internet** while a MAC address is used on a **LAN**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
When a device moves to a different network, its MAC address changes.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The **MAC address stays the same** when a device moves network; it is the **IP address** that changes.

front_blocks.md: Define **device name**.

back_blocks.md: A device name is a way for users to **describe or name a device** so that it is **easier to identify on a network**.

cards.front_md: Define **device name**.
cards.back_md: A device name is a way for users to **describe or name a device** so that it is **easier to identify on a network**.

front_blocks.md: Why are device names not used by devices to communicate?

back_blocks.md: Device names are **not always unique**; they are **set by users** in the device's operating system or from a router.

cards.front_md: Why are device names not used by devices to communicate?

front_blocks.md: Name the two most common types of cable in a wired network.

back_blocks.md: The two most common are **Ethernet** and **fibre optic**.

cards.front_md: Name the two most common types of cable in a wired network.
cards.back_md: The two most common are **Ethernet** and **fibre optic**.

front_blocks.md: What does Ethernet cable carry, and over what kind of network?

back_blocks.md: Ethernet is a wired networking standard that carries **electrical signals** between devices on a **local area network (LAN)**.

cards.front_md: What does Ethernet cable carry, and over what kind of network?
cards.back_md: Ethernet is a wired networking standard that carries **electrical signals** between devices on a **local area network (LAN)**.

front_blocks.md: Ethernet uses <u>**                    **</u> cables (CAT5) to allow duplex communication.

back_blocks.md: Ethernet uses **twisted pair** cables (CAT5) to allow duplex communication.

cards.back_md: Ethernet uses **twisted pair** cables (CAT5) to allow duplex communication.

front_blocks.md: Why is fibre optic the most secure option for sending sensitive data?

back_blocks.md: Fibre optic cable **does not suffer from interference**, and it also carries data at much higher speed and bandwidth over long distances without degradation.

cards.front_md: Why is fibre optic the most secure option for sending sensitive data?

front_blocks.md: What does a wireless access point do?

back_blocks.md: A wireless access point (WAP) **allows wireless devices to connect to a local area network**, connecting to a switch or hub via an Ethernet cable.

cards.front_md: What does a wireless access point do?
cards.back_md: A wireless access point (WAP) **allows wireless devices to connect to a local area network**, connecting to a switch or hub via an Ethernet cable.

front_blocks.md: Why might a building need more than one wireless access point?

back_blocks.md: The **range of a WAP is limited**, so multiple access points are used to give complete coverage of a home or business.

cards.front_md: Why might a building need more than one wireless access point?
cards.back_md: The **range of a WAP is limited**, so multiple access points are used to give complete coverage of a home or business.

front_blocks.md: State three tasks carried out by a router.

back_blocks.md: A router **receives packets**, **forwards packets**, **maintains a routing table**, **identifies the most efficient path** to the destination, and **assigns IP addresses** to devices.

cards.front_md: State three tasks carried out by a router.
cards.back_md: A router **receives packets**, **forwards packets**, **maintains a routing table**, **identifies the most efficient path** to the destination, and **assigns IP addresses** to devices.

front_blocks.md: Define **gateway**.

back_blocks.md: A gateway is a device that **bridges the connection between two different types of network**, translating between different network protocols.

cards.front_md: Define **gateway**.
cards.back_md: A gateway is a device that **bridges the connection between two different types of network**, translating between different network protocols.

front_blocks.md: What does a switch do, and why is it called an active device?

back_blocks.md: A switch **allows multiple wired devices to connect to a LAN**, and it is **active** because it can **inspect network data and route it to the correct device**, reducing traffic on the network.

cards.front_md: What does a switch do, and why is it called an active device?
cards.back_md: A switch **allows multiple wired devices to connect to a LAN**, and it is **active** because it can **inspect network data and route it to the correct device**, reducing traffic on the network.

front_blocks.md: What does a booster do?

back_blocks.md: A booster **amplifies a network signal** in order to **extend the normal range**, and can be used with both wired and wireless networks.

cards.front_md: What does a booster do?
cards.back_md: A booster **amplifies a network signal** in order to **extend the normal range**, and can be used with both wired and wireless networks.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A wireless access point can never act as a booster.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A wireless access point **can be configured to act as a booster**, in what is known as **repeater mode**.

front_blocks.md: Define **server**.

back_blocks.md: A server is a **dedicated computer that shares its resources** with the devices that connect to it, which are known as **clients**.

cards.front_md: Define **server**.
cards.back_md: A server is a **dedicated computer that shares its resources** with the devices that connect to it, which are known as **clients**.

front_blocks.md: Name five common types of server.

back_blocks.md: **File**, **web**, **print**, **authentication** and **application** servers.

cards.front_md: Name five common types of server.
cards.back_md: **File**, **web**, **print**, **authentication** and **application** servers.

front_blocks.md: What does an authentication server do?

back_blocks.md: It **stores usernames and passwords** that can be checked when a user logs in, and authenticated users receive a **certificate** that allows access to resources.

cards.front_md: What does an authentication server do?

front_blocks.md: What does a print server do?

back_blocks.md: A print server **manages print jobs** and **organises the queue** so that individual printers are not overloaded.

cards.front_md: What does a print server do?

front_blocks.md: Define **web browser**.

back_blocks.md: A web browser is a software application used to **locate, retrieve and display content** on the **World Wide Web**.

front_blocks.md: Name four common features of a web browser.

back_blocks.md: A **home page**, the ability to **bookmark favourites**, a **history of visited websites**, and **hyperlinks** that allow users to navigate between pages.

front_blocks.md: Define **Internet Service Provider (ISP)**.

back_blocks.md: An Internet Service Provider is a **company that provides access to the internet** to users and businesses.

front_blocks.md: How does an ISP provide internet access, and how is it paid for?

back_blocks.md: The ISP **leases equipment and telecommunication lines** to users, and generally **charges a subscription fee**.
